account: Radiolytica combines speech recognition, language models and human review to monitor French and Swahili radio. Fondation Hirondelle's 2024 annual report states that a pilot to detect hate speech with AI on community radio in Goma and Bukavu was set up in 2024. In its June 2025 account, the foundation describes a research prototype and planned expansion. On a project page for the 2025 AI Action Summit, the foundation wrote that it monitors community radio stations in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and broadcasts adapted radio content in response to the hate speech that it detects. Faster monitoring and counter-messaging are intended benefits. No source documents a response to a particular broadcast or a measured reduction in harm. The foundation's project sheet of April 2026 sets the goal of extending this monitoring to 100 radio stations in 2026 and reports no measured result.
